Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-05
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sandra Kim (Redwood), Daniel Reyes (Head of ML, Arclight), Priya Nair (CTO), Marcus Lee (SRE), Aisha Khan (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-gen):

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining... I'm Maya, AE on this.
[00:12] Daniel Reyes: yep thanks, Maya, appreciate it. we are excited to get a concrete plan.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: hi all, Liam from Redwood infra, I'll own the bench and perf side, and I'll be point for any dedicated/private run setup.
[00:26] Priya Nair: hi, Priya here, CTO. primary goal is to validate cost & latency tradeoffs for our real-time summarization pipeline.
[00:35] Marcus Lee: Marcus here — we'll handle the network and infra side, need to understand VPC peering and egress.

[01:05] Maya Patel: quick framing — typical runbook we do: kickoff (access + credentials), baseline run (hosted), dedicated run (if requested), midpoint review, then exec readout. want to confirm success criteria up front: what would success look like to you?
[01:20] Daniel Reyes: functionally we need the model to match our quality bar — roughly the same ROUGE/QA pass rate as our current on-prem model within a 3% delta. performance goals are 95th percentile latency under 300ms for 95% of requests, and cost per 1k tokens below $X — we don't have exact number but want a ballpark. also throughput needs: baseline 250 req/s sustained, burst to 600 req/s.
[01:48] Sandra Kim: quick clarification — is that 300ms at average request size or peak token size?
[01:54] Daniel Reyes: average request is about 350 tokens in, 120 tokens out; peak can go to 1,200 tokens in rare flows. so SLO should be qualified by token distribution.
[02:10] Liam O'Connor: good, we'll ask for a token histogram. For the bench we'll run three profiles: short (<=100t), med (~350t), long (1000-1200t). we'll report P50/P95/P99 latencies and tokens/sec.

[03:00] Priya Nair: we also care about cold-start behavior, warm cache performance, and failure modes — if a model variant is unavailable we need graceful fallback to lighter model.
[03:12] Maya Patel: yes, Redwood supports routing policies and model fallbacks; we'll demonstrate canary/fallback in the dedicated test.

[04:05] Marcus Lee: security — we need SOC 2 type II evidence, SSO/SAML support, audit logs, and optional KMS integration for keys. for private deployment we might require on-prem or VPC with peered subnets.
[04:23] Sandra Kim: noted, we have a security pack and SOC 2 docs; I'll link those. KMS/HSM is supported with customer-managed keys, but for the POC we can do ephemeral keys and then upgrade.

[05:10] Maya Patel: timeline proposal: Kickoff this week (access + onboarding) -> baseline benchmarks week 2 -> dedicated run / quantized model tests week 3 -> midpoint review end of week 3 -> iterate and finalize benchmarks week 4 -> exec readout target week 5. propose concrete dates in next-steps.
[05:30] Daniel Reyes: sounds reasonable. what's the expected duration for the baseline bench run?
[05:35] Liam O'Connor: baseline run usually takes 48-72 hours to capture warm-up, steady state, and some burst windows. dedicated runs similar but need provisioning window (24 hours) once we confirm instance sizes.

[06:20] Aisha Khan: on metrics — beyond latency and cost we want quality checks: a small eval harness that flags hallucination rates, top-k stability, and regeneration variance. can you run those as part of the bench?
[06:34] Liam O'Connor: yes, we can wire up your eval set into the harness. we'll run automated prompts and compute delta against your golden set. also we can store the artifact logs for post-analysis.

[07:00] Daniel Reyes: for data privacy — some sample data is PII; can Redwood run the bench within our VPC or do we need to mask data?
[07:10] Maya Patel: options: (1) hosted sandbox with NDA and ephemeral creds for deidentified data, (2) Redwood Dedicated with DB access and isolation, (3) Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) for full data residency. for POC, VPC peering usually suffices.
[07:32] Marcus Lee: we'll explore VPC peering first. will need network CIDRs and contact to set up peering.

[08:00] Liam O'Connor: technical bench details: we'll run the Redwood runtime in both quantized and fp16 modes where supported; measure throughput for batching sizes 1-8; and record memory/KV cache behavior. also we'll report on per-token cost and cost per 1k responses.
[08:20] Maya Patel: call out gating criteria — we recommend three acceptance gates for the POC: (1) Functional parity (quality within agreed delta), (2) Perf SLOs met (P95 latency threshold + throughput), (3) Cost threshold within agreed percent of target. If any gate fails we capture remediation actions.

[09:15] Priya Nair: who owns the decision to pass the POC? is it a combined sign-off?
[09:20] Maya Patel: typically it's a joint signoff: Arclight exec + Redwood AE/SE sign. we'll prepare an exec readout pack highlighting pass/fail criteria.

[10:05] Daniel Reyes: logistics: we'll need the harness code and a reproducible script. are you able to share the bench code?
[10:12] Liam O'Connor: yes, we'll share a github repo with the harness, Dockerfile, and instructions. we can also offer to run it on your infra if preferred.

[11:00] Maya Patel: access checklist for kickoff: 1) sample dataset + token distribution; 2) user for test tenant or org SSO; 3) network contact for peering if doing VPC; 4) expected exec attendees for readout.
[11:18] Daniel Reyes: I'll get those items queued; Marcus will reach out on peering.

[12:05] Sandra Kim: security docs note: I'll send SOC 2 summary, encryption at rest docs, and our audit log format. expect an email after this call.

[13:00] Aisha Khan: about the exec readout content — can we preview a template so we know what success artifacts we need to produce?
[13:12] Maya Patel: yes we'll include a sample exec readout deck: objectives, metrics, benchmark tables, cost sensitivity, risk & mitigations, suggested next steps. we'll attach that to the invite.

[14:05] Marcus Lee: for dedicated runs, what sizes do you recommend? we anticipate the model is roughly 7B-13B parameter family but we're still onboarding which variant we'll use.
[14:18] Liam O'Connor: for 7B-class with quantization we typically test on a single A100/80GB equivalent for early stage; for 13B we'd recommend 2x 80GB or a multi-GPU config depending on seq length. we'll provide exact instance recommendations after we see your token distribution.

[15:00] Daniel Reyes: curious about cost math — can you provide a rough per-1k-token delta between hosted vs dedicated?
[15:08] Maya Patel: we'll produce a comparative cost sheet in the baseline report; very rough rule: hosted is faster to start but per-token unit cost is higher; dedicated brings down unit cost at predictable throughput but has reservation or infra commitment. exact deltas depend on batch and cache hit rates.

[16:00] Priya Nair: any risks where the model behavior changes across quantization? we need to evaluate quality degradation with int8 or awq.
[16:10] Liam O'Connor: yes, quantization can shift generation slightly. we'll include A/B of fp16 vs int8/awq using your eval prompts and compute deltas on key metrics. if quality falls outside gate we won't recommend that config for production.

[17:05] Maya Patel: proposed milestone calendar (dates tentative):
- Kickoff: 2025-11-07 (access + onboarding)
- Baseline hosted bench start: 2025-11-10 to 2025-11-12 (48-72h)
- Dedicated/quantized tests: 2025-11-13 to 2025-11-16
- Midpoint review: 2025-11-25 (internal detailed readout)
- Finalization and remediation: 2025-11-26 to 2025-11-29
- Exec readout: target 2025-12-05

[18:00] Daniel Reyes: that gives us time to polish results before execs. works for us pending calendar checks.

[19:10] Maya Patel: I'll send a calendar with milestones and invites for the midpoint review and exec readout — please mark the exec readout as "Decision point" in the title.

[20:05] Sandra Kim: action items recap: I'll drop security pack; Liam will drop bench repo; Maya will provision tenant and send onboarding; Daniel will send datasets & token hist; Marcus will share peering contacts.

[21:00] Priya Nair: one last question — if a gate fails at midpoint, do we get extension or is POC considered failed?
[21:10] Maya Patel: typical approach is to document remediation plan and run a follow-up short remediation sprint; we aim for a collaborative outcome rather than binary pass/fail. exec readout will present both status and recommended next steps.

[22:00] Daniel Reyes: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the dataset and confirm peering next week.

[22:20] Maya Patel: thanks all — we'll share the onboarding + timeline doc after the call and ping for dates.

[22:30] (recording ends)
